title: Ask HN: Advice on local efficient analogical retrieval?
summary:
So.. I've been running my own archive of conversations, voice recordings, documents, and etc for AI agents (mostly Claude Code) for past 6 month.

Currently, when i ask or it answers something it runs hook that checks previous conversations, lists up potential related conversations.

The intention is not only to retreive relative memories, but also to be able to connect 2 or more conversations that looks irrelevant but extract some kind of pattern or insight from it. In other words, I want my model to partially go off on a tangent, in a good way...

For example; Let's say I bring up topic on investing on OKLO as a potential 10x company. So I say I will keep it small but don't cut loss, only buy more from time to time. I want model to be able to bring up the memory that I also regularly buy things from my few favorite small restuarants just to keep them alive. Maybe connect those 2, and be able to tell that in perspective, I may have a consistant view on spending money. I even have few conversations on that exact topic as well. It just doesn't use similar keywords.

I feel like maybe the obstacle is that model can't come up with the direction that the conversation could develop to a broader(or deeper) topic on my philosophy on capital? I'm not sure.

These are the list I've tried: 1. Personalized PageRank 2. Hebbian edge reinforcement(between opened conversation) 3. character n-gram TF-IDF similarity 4.contrastive embedding trained on my conversation 5. query expansion over a word co-occurrence graph 6. matching on shared verbs 7. serendipity slot 8. simple agentic search 9. abstracting each message into a domain-free sentence 10. keword search + LLM judgement 11. BGE-M3

All these can't quite achieve to the point I describe. It certainly works well getting related memory.

The search should be fast, light, because reading the history itself takes time, so can't really afford long search time on top of that. I run this on multi device, so it should be portable friendly.

Any advice or idea on this approach? public version of the repo: https://github.com/milez770/madeleine

title: Tell HN: Don't use Postman, they proxy your info without your permission
summary:
When you send a POST request to your server, you think you're sending the information to YOUR server, right? That was the default behaviour - as it should be. After updating the Postman client, I noticed Postman also sends the request to their internal servers, which then sends your server the actual request (proxying). I thought I was paranoid until another commenter confirmed the same (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50358055). It's fucking annoying that something called POSTman does anything but that. Please don't use Postman for anything sensitive. It's borderline spyware, especially when you didn't consent to this behavior.

title: Ask HN: What is Google Flights' business model and has it changed recently?
summary:
I'm wondering if anyone has any more info than I do regarding why Google offers Google Flights? As far as I know there's no paid version of the software and Google doesn't take a cut of any sales they refer. It seems like it must cost Google a fair amount of money to run and doesn't have any direct revenue source.

I also wonder if anything has shifted recently - I think Google Flights has been around for over a decade, and for most of that time it felt aligned with my interests - simplifying the process of finding the cheapest flights to get me where I want to go.

Unfortunately, it has recently seemed degraded in several ways.

1) It doesn't reliably offer round-trips made of 2 one-way tickets from 2 different airlines.

2) It doesn't reliably pick up new destinations. I recently saw an airline added a route that would allow me to reach a desired destination in 2 segments rather than 3. I excitedly searched for such itineraries and couldn't find them on Google Flights (but I could on the website for the airline, whose flights are generally on Google Flights).

3) I live in an area served by multiple airports. Similar to my first issue, I feel like Google Flights no longer reliably shows me round-trip itineraries that depart from one airport and arrive an another (e.g. depart from Heathrow, arrive back in London at Gatwick). Once I pick a departure airport it

Is it just me hitting some bugs or hiccups? Or is Google actively degrading Google Flights for some reason (too expensive?). Is Google trying to simplify things for naive users? Or is Google Flights abandonware within Google that is running without much ongoing support?

title: Gitbook Breached
summary:
We opened a ticket with support about Gitbook availability issues and got this in reply. We have yet to see any official customer communication or breach notification. Apologies for the formatting, did the best I could as it's a mobile paste.

Update:

GitBook security incident update Hey <$name>, The GitBook app, the GitBook API, and published docs are available again. A few services may still be degraded as we finish restoring everything to full performance.

*What happened* GitBook has been the target of a sophisticated, highly targeted attack using AI agents. At 19:00 CET, November 2, the attacker gained unauthorized access to some of our infrastructure credentials. We detected the attack immediately and acted swiftly to block further impact. To make sure our infrastructure was fully secure, we then took the GitBook app and authenticated docs sites offline. We kept publicly published content live for as long as possible, using cached data.

*What we did immediately* * Blocked the attacker and closed the vulnerabilities involved * Replaced every credential and secret across our infrastructure * Brought services back only once we were confident they were secure * Invalidated every customer’s API tokens on our platform

*Your data* Our investigation shows that the attacker may have accessed the following: * Git Sync secrets. * GitBook API tokens. * Third-party API tokens used to connect external tools to GitBook. * Questions asked to GitBook Assistant by your site visitors.

At this stage, we have found no evidence that any of your content in GitBook was modified.

*What you need to do now* * Rotate any existing GitBook API tokens. We revoked all personal API tokens during the incident. * Rotate any third-party API tokens or secrets you use to connect other tools to GitBook. * If you have published integrations that use secrets, rotate those secrets. * If you use the GitBook MCP server, re-authenticate it. Please contact your GitBook organization’s admin to assist with this process.

*What we are doing next* * Monitoring the situation in case of further attacks. * Introducing further security measures to our platform. * Writing a full post mortem that will be published soon with more detailed information about the incident. * If you have any further questions, please reach out to your account manager or our support team. You can also check status.gitbook.com for updates

Thank you for your patience, and we apologize again for the disruption The GitBook team
